title: Russia Launches 272 Shahed Drones Overnight; Ukraine Intercepts 249 — Odessa Port, Zaporizhzhia Plant, Sumy Hit — Day 1,563
detail: Overnight June 5–6, 2026 (Day 1,563), Russia launched 272 Shahed-type kamikaze drones across Ukraine; Ukrainian air defense destroyed 249 of them. Impacts were confirmed at 11 locations. Key strikes included: the port infrastructure in Odessa; the Kryvorizka thermal power plant in Zelenodolsk (Dnipropetrovsk Oblast); the Zaporizhzhia Machine-Building Plant; Zaporizhzhia city, where a drone strike sparked a parking-lot fire and 7 people sought medical care; Sumy region, where guided aerial bombs killed one man; and Dnipropetrovsk region (1 killed, 3 wounded). During the daytime of June 6, Russia launched 46 additional airstrikes with 134 guided aerial bombs and 6,064 kamikaze drones, and conducted 2,445 artillery strikes. A total of 183 combat collisions were recorded. The Pokrovsk direction saw 26 Russian attacks. Russian MoD claimed control of Shevchenko village in Kharkiv region. The overnight attack followed the pattern of Russia's sustained aerial-terror campaign against Ukrainian civilian infrastructure and industrial targets.

media.caption: Russian 272-drone overnight attack on Ukraine, June 5–6 — 249 intercepted, Odessa port, Zaporizhzhia plant, Sumy and Dnipropetrovsk hit

title: Ukraine Strikes Kronstadt Naval Base with ~376 Drones; Hits Baltic Fleet 15th Arsenal, Submarine R&D Institute — Final Day of Putin's SPIEF — Day 1,563
detail: On the night of June 5–6, 2026 (Day 1,563), Ukraine's Special Operations Forces, Unmanned Systems Forces (SBS), and the SBU launched approximately 376 drones in a large-scale deep strike against military infrastructure in the St. Petersburg and Leningrad region — approximately 1,000 km from Ukraine's border. Primary confirmed targets included: Kronstadt Naval Base (Baltic Fleet), specifically striking naval arsenals and the Kronstadt Marine Plant; the Russian Navy's 15th Arsenal at Bolshaya Izhora, which stores naval ammunition and armaments, with secondary detonations confirmed; the Research Institute of Marine Thermal Engineering in Lomonosov district — a key facility for submarine-launched torpedo and missile R&D — where a fire broke out and partial resident evacuation was ordered; and the Ust-Labinsk oil depot in Krasnodar Krai, approximately 500 km from the Ukrainian border. Russia claimed to have intercepted 144 drones in the Leningrad/St. Petersburg area; a second Russian claim cited 141 intercepts in Leningrad Oblast specifically. Three people sustained minor injuries on the Russian side. Open-source satellite imagery confirmed fire at the Kronstadt base territory and smoke over the Kronstadt Marine Plant. The strikes coincided with the final day of the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF) — Putin's flagship economic summit. Zelensky framed the operation as 'long-range sanctions' and called on Russia to end the war: 'It is time to end this war. But Russia's ruler wants to keep fighting.' This second large-scale Kronstadt strike in four days (following the June 3 strike that set corvette Boikiy ablaze) represented a sustained campaign to degrade Russia's Baltic Fleet infrastructure and naval production capacity.

media.caption: Ukraine strikes Kronstadt Naval Base with ~376 drones — Baltic Fleet 15th Arsenal hit, submarine R&D institute damaged, fires confirmed

title: Ukraine's 3rd SOF Regiment Establishes Aerial Drone Control Over Melitopol–Chonhar Crimea Supply Route — Day 1,563
detail: On June 6, 2026 (Day 1,563), Ukraine's 3rd Separate Special Purpose Regiment (Special Operations Forces) announced that it had established aerial drone control over the Melitopol–Chonhar road — the critical land supply corridor connecting Russian-occupied mainland Ukraine to Russian-occupied Crimea. The regiment stated: 'Drones of the Special Operations Forces unit are destroying equipment and breaking the enemy's logistics routes on the Melitopol-Chonhar route… This is just the beginning. More to come.' The Melitopol-Chonhar route is one of only three logistics corridors to Crimea: the Kerch Bridge (road and rail), the Donetsk rail/road corridor through Melitopol, and the narrow Chonhar crossing over the Syvash — a shallow lagoon with only narrow bridge crossings over flat steppe terrain. The open steppe geography makes vehicles in transit extremely vulnerable to FPV drone and loitering munition attack. This announcement escalated Ukraine's systematic drone interdiction campaign against Russian logistics to Crimea, which had already created fuel shortages on the peninsula from prior drone strikes on Crimea's storage infrastructure. The June 6 announcement preceded a direct Chonhar bridge strike the following day (June 7), which suspended traffic through the Dzhankoi checkpoint, demonstrating that the aerial interdiction campaign was coordinated and multi-day.

media.caption: Ukraine's 3rd SOF Regiment announces aerial drone control over Melitopol–Chonhar Crimea supply corridor, setting stage for bridge strike

title: Putin Meets Former German Chancellor Schröder at Kremlin as Proposed Mediator; EU and Kyiv Reject His Candidacy — Day 1,563
detail: On June 5–6, 2026 (Day 1,563), Russian President Vladimir Putin met privately at the Kremlin with former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder, who has been proposed as a potential mediator between Russia and Europe in any future peace settlement. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the meeting as 'good and friendly' but disclosed no specifics. Schröder, who served as German Chancellor 1998–2005, has maintained close ties with Russia after leaving office — he holds senior positions at Russian state energy companies, including Rosneft, and was a longtime personal friend of Putin. The meeting occurred one day after Zelensky published his open letter challenging Putin to direct talks. EU Foreign Policy Chief Kaja Kallas sharply rejected Schröder as a mediator: 'It is clear why Putin wants him — he would be sitting on both sides of the table.' Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated that Kyiv 'definitely does not support such a candidacy.' The Schröder meeting illustrated Russia's preference for back-channel diplomacy excluding Ukraine's Western supporters, in contrast to Zelensky's call for direct talks with EU leaders present. The meeting followed Putin's public rejection of Zelensky's ceasefire conditions.

media.caption: Putin meets Schröder at Kremlin: proposed mediator rejected by EU's Kallas and Ukrainian FM Sybiha as conflict of interest
